title: How to Spot a Fake W-8BEN
summary: Spot a fake W-8BEN by reading foreign status, the treaty claim, and the file. The IRS publishes a blank and does not certify the form.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Form W-8BEN is the certificate an individual gives a withholding agent to establish foreign status for U.S. tax withholding. The[IRS instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw8ben) (revised October 2021) set the default rate at 30 percent on U.S.-source fixed or determinable income when that status is undocumented. A seal or a typed name on the signature line fails as a visual check, because the IRS publishes a blank and the individual completes it. The file was either edited after that person signed or generated as a finished form.


## What a Fake W-8BEN Actually Is


A W-8BEN is the individual's own certificate.[About Form W-8BEN](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-8-ben) states the use: a foreign person who is the beneficial owner gives the form to the withholding agent or payer, whether or not a reduced rate is claimed. The October 2021 form stays with the agent.


The instructions limit the form to individuals. An entity documents foreign status on Form W-8BEN-E, which belongs with the entity file covered in[KYB document fraud detection](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/kyb-document-fraud-detection) . A U.S. citizen, including one living abroad, and a resident alien document status on Form W-9, covered in[how to spot a fake W-9](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-w-9) . A W-8BEN certifies status. A return reports income, covered in[how to spot a fake tax return](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-tax-return) .


A W-8BEN generally remains in effect from the signature date through the last day of the third succeeding calendar year, unless a change in circumstances makes any information incorrect. A form signed on September 30, 2015, remains valid through December 31, 2018. Some certificates remain in effect longer, until a change in circumstances. An expired form is a documentation failure. The fraud question opens when dates or identity fields were rewritten to keep an old certificate inside the window.


The upload arrives in two production classes. Edited-after-creation starts from a real signed W-8BEN, a prior year's form, or the IRS blank, then changes the name, the country, the permanent residence address, the treaty claim, or the signature date. Generated-from-scratch fills every line, including a signature, so the page agrees with itself and never passed through the individual. The instructions treat a signature as electronic when it shows that an authorized person signed, for example with a time and date stamp and a statement that the form was electronically signed. A name typed on the signature line, with nothing else, fails that test.


A third class is a phishing form aimed at the individual. The IRS page on[fake Form W-8BEN scams](https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/fake-form-w-8ben-used-in-irs-tax-scams) says those forms ask for a mother's maiden name, a passport number, or a PIN. The legitimate form leaves those fields off.


## Tells That Still Work, and the Ones That Do Not


Six tells on a W-8BEN, from the seal to serial reuse.


The story on the face of the form still works when it is read against the rest of the file. Part I names the individual, citizenship, permanent residence, a foreign tax identifying number, and a date of birth. Part II, when completed, names the treaty country. Part III is the certification, signed and dated by the beneficial owner or by an agent with authority.


An IRS seal, a watermark, and a form number fail as proof that anyone issued this completed page.


A permanent residence address in the United States, or a post office box offered as that residence, conflicts with a claim of foreign residence. The instructions place that address in the country where the individual claims to be a resident for that country's income tax, and they exclude a post office box, a financial institution's address, and an address used only for mailing. A treaty claim names a country that has an income tax treaty with the United States. With limited exceptions, including certain students and researchers, that country and the permanent residence address are the same place.


Identity sits on a different document.[FinCEN's CDD rule](https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/cdd-final-rule) requires covered institutions to identify and verify the customer. For beneficial owners of legal entity customers, the institution collects a name, a date of birth, an address, and an identification number, using a passport or similar document for a foreign person. A W-8BEN supplies a self-certification of status. The passport in[identity document verification for customer onboarding](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/identity-document-verification-for-customer-onboarding) still does the identity work. Agreement between the form and the passport still leaves the PDF untested.


Tell What it still catches What it misses


IRS seal, watermark, or form number Almost nothing on a completed individual certificate Genuine electronic forms and generated forms


A U.S. person or an entity on this form A citizen, resident alien, or company using the individual certificate A foreign individual on the correct form


Residence, citizenship, and treaty country versus the passport A status claim the identity file does not support A consistent packet produced together


A signature that is only a typed name A certification the instructions do not treat as signed An electronic signature with a time stamp and a signing statement


Maiden name, passport number, or PIN on the form A phishing form the legitimate W-8BEN does not use A real certificate, which correctly omits those fields


The same signed PDF across unrelated people Serial reuse of one certificate The first time that file appears


## How Detection Actually Works


The file's story is that this individual completed a W-8BEN, signed and dated the certification, and claimed foreign status, plus a treaty benefit if Part II is filled in.


Production method asks how the page was made. Edited-after-creation leaves a real certification under a later save, usually at the name, the country, the address, the treaty lines, or the signature date. Generated-from-scratch has no individual submission underneath. The case note should name the class. A typed form is neither class by itself when the electronic signature carries a time and date stamp and a statement that the form was signed.


Timestamp trail asks whether creation and modification fit the signature date. A form signed in March and saved again in October can be the agent's copy. A signature dated last week on a file built months earlier around a different country reads as an edit. A date inside the validity window can still be a date written onto an older file.


Issuer matching is easy to aim at the wrong office. The individual completes the form. The IRS publishes the blank and does not certify the finished page. A file styled as an IRS determination misses the use the instructions describe: give the form to the withholding agent or payer. Reliance on a completed certificate leaves open whether this PDF is the page that individual signed.


Consistency checks the name, citizenship, permanent residence address, date of birth, foreign tax identifying number, and any treaty country against the identity document and the application. A generated form will obey the line labels on its face. The break is a residence address in one country, a treaty claim for another, and a passport for a third, or a date of birth that disagrees with the identity file.


Model artifacts are certification prose, part headings, and signature images that come from neither the IRS blank nor a real signing record. Extra fields such as a mother's maiden name, a passport number, or a PIN match the phishing form the IRS has described. Recycled patterns are the same signed PDF or the same signature image on an unrelated individual.


## What to Do with a Suspect File


Hold the account and the reduced withholding rate. Read the name, citizenship, permanent residence address, date of birth, signature, and signature date. If Part II is completed, read the treaty country against that address and against the identity document. An entity belongs on Form W-8BEN-E. A U.S. person belongs on Form W-9. A form that asks for a passport number, a PIN, or a mother's maiden name is the phishing variant.


Count the validity window from the signature date through the last day of the third succeeding calendar year. An expired form is a reason to request a new certificate. The fraud question opens when that date was moved, or when the country or the treaty lines changed after the certification was applied.


When the face of the form agrees with the passport and the file still looks rewritten, ask whether the name, the address, or the treaty claim changed after the signature. For a scored read of the file itself,[check the file](https://sphinxhq.com/products/doc-fraud) . The x-ray is production method, timestamps, issuer match, consistency, model artifacts, and recycled patterns. The passport remains the identity check. The form remains the status certificate.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How can you tell if a W-8BEN is fake?


Compare the name, citizenship, permanent residence address, date of birth, and any treaty country with the identity document. Confirm the certification is signed and dated as the IRS instructions recognize, inside the validity window. Competent fakes fail when a field was edited after the individual signed, or when the whole form was generated and never signed by that person.


### What is the difference between a W-8BEN and a W-9?


Form W-8BEN is the certificate of foreign status an individual gives the withholding agent. Form W-9 is the certification a U.S. person, including a citizen living abroad, gives when an information return is required. An entity uses Form W-8BEN-E.


### How long is a Form W-8BEN valid?


The October 2021 instructions say a W-8BEN generally remains in effect from the signature date through the last day of the third succeeding calendar year, unless a change in circumstances makes any information incorrect. A form signed on September 30, 2015, remained valid through December 31, 2018.


### Does the IRS issue a completed W-8BEN?


The IRS publishes the blank Form W-8BEN and the instructions. The individual completes it and gives it to the withholding agent or payer. A completed form with no IRS certification stamp is the ordinary document.


### What if a W-8BEN asks for a passport number or a PIN?


The legitimate Form W-8BEN leaves off a passport number, a PIN, and a mother's maiden name. The IRS describes forms that ask for those as scams aimed at non-residents. Identity still comes from the passport or other identity document in the onboarding file.
